terms.meaning: The Highest Common Factor: the largest number that divides all the given numbers.
The Lowest Common Multiple: the smallest number that all the given numbers divide.
Numbers whose HCF is 1. They have no common prime factor.

items.name: Prime factorisation
items.formula: Write the number as a product of primes

items.name: Factors from prime factors
items.formula: Every factor is a product of some of its prime factors

items.name: LCM from prime factors
items.formula: Take each prime the most times it appears in any number

items.name: HCF and LCM together
items.formula: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers

items.name: Largest size that fits exactly
items.example: The largest square tile for a 12 ft by 16 ft room has side 4 ft.

items.name: Fewest equal bags
items.formula: Use the HCF as the bag size
items.example: 84 kg and 108 kg: bags of 12 kg, so 7 + 9 = 16 bags.

items.name: When things happen together
items.example: Every 7 days and every 10 days: they match every 70 days.

mistakes.text: Do not swap them. The HCF is never more than the smaller number, and the LCM is never less than the larger one.
The LCM need not be the product. For 6 and 8 the LCM is 24, not 48. It equals the product only for co-prime numbers.
HCF × LCM = product works for two numbers, not always for three. For 2, 4, 8: 2 × 8 = 16, but the product is 64.
